verdicts.title: Exact Ramsey Theory: Green-Tao numbers and SAT
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We consider the links between Ramsey theory in the integers, based on van der Waerden's theorem, and (boolean, CNF) SAT solving. We aim at using the problems from exact Ramsey theory, concerned with computing Ramsey-type numbers, as a rich source of test problems, where especially methods for solving hard problems can be developed. In order to control the growth of the problem instances, we introduce "transversal extensions" as a natural way of constructing mixed parameter tuples (k_1, ..., k_m)
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns Ramsey theory, van der Waerden/Green-Tao numbers, and SAT encodings for benchmarking solvers — it makes no claim about tiling system ranks, arithmetic circuit size, or unate polynomial degree bounds for boolean circuits.

verdicts.title: Dsat: A Native SAT Solver for Discrete Logic
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Discrete variables are common in many applications, such as probabilistic reasoning, planning and explainable AI. When symbolic reasoning techniques are brought in to bear on these applications, a standard technique for handling discrete variables is to binarize them into Boolean variables to allow the use of Boolean computational machinery such as SAT solvers. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a native SAT solver for discrete logic variables ('a native SAT solver for discrete logic, which is a direct extension of Boolean logic'), which shares only the general SAT/Boolean framework vocabulary but says nothing about tiling systems, arithmetic circuit ranks, or unate polynomial degree bounds.

verdicts.title: Generating and Searching Families of FFT Algorithms
